did_you_know.text: Did you know? Daniel chapter 1 opens in the third year of King Jehoiakim’s reign, when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against Jerusalem and besieged it.

Did you know? According to the chapter, Jehoiakim and some of the vessels from the house of God were handed over to Nebuchadnezzar, and the vessels were brought to the land of Shinar and placed in the treasury of his god.
Did you know? Nebuchadnezzar ordered that some Israelites be brought—those from the royal family and from the nobles, meaning families of high status—to be trained for service in the king’s court.

Did you know? The young men chosen had to be without physical defect, good-looking, intelligent, knowledgeable, and capable of serving in the king’s palace; they were to be taught the writing and language of the Chaldeans.
Did you know? The chief official gave Daniel and his companions new names: Daniel was called Belteshazzar, Hananiah Shadrach, Mishael Meshach, and Azariah Abednego.
Did you know? Daniel resolved not to defile himself with the king’s food or the wine he drank, and he asked for permission to avoid them.

Did you know? Daniel proposed a ten-day test to the steward: he and his companions would eat vegetables and drink water, after which their appearance would be compared with that of the young men who ate the king’s food.
Did you know? God gave the four young men knowledge and understanding in every kind of writing and wisdom, and Daniel also had the ability to understand visions and dreams.
Did you know? When the king examined them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters throughout his kingdom.
Did you know? The chapter states that Daniel continued until the first year of King Cyrus.
